papers.title: On the Configuration-LP for Scheduling on Unrelated Machines
papers.pdf_version: arXiv v1 submitted 2010-11-22; ESA2011 conference; Journal of Scheduling 17(4), 2014
papers.location: Theorem 2, manuscript printed p. 4 statement and p. 7 proof (PDF pp. 5,8); Lemmas 4–6 in Section 3
papers.result: Configuration LP has supremum integrality gap 2 even if each job is allowed on at most two machines with machine-dependent sizes.
papers.scope: Unrelated graph balancing; not equal-edge-size graph balancing. A family approaches 2; no finite instance with exactly ratio 2 is asserted.
papers.mechanism: Two rooted k-ary trees, each job incident to parent and child machines, plus a job joining roots; proof constructs fractional configurations recursively. Lower bound at parameter k is (2-1/k)/(1+1/k), converging to 2.
limitations: ArXiv v1 Section3.1 uses alpha1=1/(k-1) in Lemma5 but Lemma6 writes alpha_n=q^n/(k-1); with height1 as base, reconstruction uses alpha_h=q^(h-1)/(k-1). Choose h=min{h>=1:alpha_h>=1/2}, k>=4, adding one level relative to the literal N threshold when needed. This is an explicit indexing repair, not a claim the original text uses this indexing.

For alpha_h>=1/2, delete the incoming root job from a suitable fraction of root configurations to reduce its marginal to exactly1/2; downward closure preserves all other marginals and load feasibility.

reconstruction_parameters.internal_configuration_weights: Csmall has weight 1-k*alpha_child/(k-1); each {incoming, child_edge_l} has weight alpha_child/(k-1). At height1 alpha_child=1/k.
reconstruction_parameters.leaf_configuration_weights: At each terminal machine, each singleton parallel job has weight1/k.
reconstruction_parameters.top_trimming: For original configuration containing root incoming job, keep that job with probability 1/(2*alpha_h), otherwise delete only that job.
